title: Content problems found during the docs prose pass
description:
Content problems found while deslopping the docs (Mark 2026-11-27: "all the human readable text docs in mimid need the same treatment"). The pass is prose only, so each of these was left for a content decision. Separate beads already cover README's crate table (mimid-08mr) and client-survey.md's settled open question (mimid-0xot).

## mimi-catchup.md

Bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.1 is cited for two different things: §4 attaches the HTTP-header choice to it, which is decided, and §7.1 attaches the unsettled hash-chain-entry question to it, which §12.4 also points at. One bead id carrying both a settled decision and an open question is either two beads or a stale citation.

§10, the hub side, says to "record, per room and provider, the sequence ranges that provider was entitled to (§8)". §8.3 says mimid records no such thing: the bound is read off the `room_fanout` rows, and "Nothing separate records who was in the room when." §10 reads like the plan from before `room_fanout` existed. One of the two sections is wrong about what the code does.
notes:
## didwebvh-appdata-spike.md

The outcome note dated 2026-11-18 says the code-point switch is gone since bead mimid-1wgh.4.81.34, while the body describes the switch in the present tense throughout, including 'About 350 lines for the switch' and 'Replacing the extension form instead of adding a switch would delete more than it adds'. The note's own disclaimer covers it, so it is stale by design rather than wrong, but 'What it costs' and 'What the hub no longer needs' now describe two different code states. Either the body is rewritten for the state after the switch, or the disclaimer says which sections it covers.
## binary-live-stream-findings.md

F6 contradicts itself. Its **JMAP binding** says mimid uses the JMAP metadata extension's `privateMetadata` on the Chat under its own namespace (decision mimid-1wgh.63; crates/mimid-agent-core/src/client.rs:431-447). Its **Built** line says mimid does not use `privateMetadata`. The code sides with the first: `ACCEPTED_NAMESPACE` and `privateMetadata/{ACCEPTED_NAMESPACE}` in crates/mimid-agent-core/src/client.rs, the assertion on `chat["privateMetadata"]["mimid.reviewcommit.com"]` in crates/mimid-agent-core/tests/own_devices.rs:385, and crates/mimid-server/src/jmap/metadata.rs. The Built line's "nothing to build" may be right while its reason is wrong.

F8's JMAP binding clause reads inverted: "mimid adds `status` ... and the agent requires it, so a strict client of the draft alone would fail against a server that leaves it out". A client written to the draft alone has no reason to fail when `status` is absent; what it would meet is the added field. "leaves it out" looks like it should be "adds it", and the agent's own case is already in the next clause.
## nostr-comparison.md

§4(b) says "Two OpenMLS copies in one binary may build but double the MLS code". MDK pins OpenMLS at rev 6100df3 and mimid the MarkAtwood fork at f1680d9: the same crate name at two revisions, which Cargo refuses rather than builds unless one is renamed. If that is right, the puppet-mode cost is not "double the MLS code" but "will not link", and relay mode is the only option rather than the preferred one.

§1.2 says Marmot's components are in the private-use range 0x8001 to 0x800f and lists nine purposes. The device-tag component is cited elsewhere as 0x800f and lifecycle as 0x800c, so the range holds, but nine names against sixteen code points reads as an incomplete list.
## air-api-comparison.md

§2.1's `WelcomeInfo` row and §7 cite "MIMI protocol-06". AGENTS.md pins draft-ietf-mimi-protocol at -07, and the spec text in ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs is -07. Either the note records what was checked on 2026-11-21 and should say so, or the comparison needs redoing against -07.

§1.3's last bullet is labelled "**Membership changes the DS initiates.**" but describes `DeleteGroup` writing a tombstone into the group context, which the client initiates and which is not a membership change. The label does not match its paragraph.
## didwebvh-draft-feedback.md

Item 31's heading says "A member without AppDataUpdate blocks revocation" while its body says "A revocation is never blocked this way, but every record change drops these members." The heading is true of the draft as written, since OpenMLS refuses every record change while such a member is present, and false of mimid as it now stands. A heading is a citation target, so it was left; it needs either a Status line or a decision to reword it.

Section 7 point 2 says "items 2 to 10 and 13" and then gives ten parenthetical labels for nine items, because item 3 covers both JSON Lines and inside-line whitespace and item 6 both domain syntax and IDNA. Loose rather than wrong.
## frontend-auth.md

§7.1 contradicts §3.3 about what a failed plain login costs. §7.1: "each failed plain login may run the SCRAM-SHA-256 derivation once per unrevoked credential (§3.3)". §3.3's one-salt decision: "A plain login then costs one PBKDF2 derivation however many credentials there are, compared with each StoredKey" -- one derivation plus N constant-time comparisons. §7.1 reads as if it predates the one-salt decision, and it is the stated reason for the per-source slowdown, so the reasoning behind a rate limit rests on it. (§3.3's argon2id paragraph is right to say once per credential, since argon2id would need a per-credential salt.)

§4.6's IRC row says the agent "still offers `sasl=PLAIN`" while §4.1 and the §4 table say CAP LS advertises `sasl=PLAIN,SCRAM-SHA-256` after decision A3. The row's point is that `soju.im/account-required` is withheld, so the mechanism list may be stale shorthand.

§9's intro says the sizes "matter now only for the two steps still to come" while the table carries a size for every step, including the built ones.
## purple-mimi.md

§5.4 says `mimi_shutdown` "waits up to 5 seconds (INVENTED)" for every account to close by the release path of §6.3, while that path's own grace period in §6.3 item 8 is 10 s. A shutdown can therefore cut a release the release path says it will wait 10 s for. Both numbers are marked INVENTED.

§4's third limitation was a fragment in HEAD: "Every line count and binary size is an estimate. The libpurple 3 findings hold for 2.98.0 and may change with each monthly alpha. mappings are designs; the libpurple 3 parts hold for 2.98.0." The last clause had lost its subject and restated the sentence before it. It now reads "Every line count and binary size is an estimate. The libpurple API mappings are designs. The libpurple 3 findings hold for 2.98.0 and may change with each monthly alpha." The words "libpurple API" are a reconstruction of the lost subject; confirm that is what was meant.

PQ7's trailing clause, "The question had proposed a bead outside the epic with no order, and one token per Pidgin in the README meanwhile; there is no meanwhile now", was dropped. The rejected alternative survives as a property ("not a bead outside the epic with no order") and the one-token-per-Pidgin fact is in §8.1, §12.2 and §12.5.
